We found that as expected the voltage at MPP kept relatively constant for the control and TPPO-containing device while increasing slightly with the BOP-Cl device (Figure 2.2b). However, the photocurrents followed the trend of the power conversion efficiency (Figure 2.2c). This observation suggests that, with phosphine oxide derivatives, we were able to reduce ion migration and ionic losses such that the initial burn in photocurrent caused by the field screening effect of ionic migration was mostly eliminated. The control device dropped from 22.4% to 19.2% (~86%) after 550 hours of aging while the TPPO-based device dropped from 22.3% to 19.1% (~86%) after 1,200 hours of aging and the BOP-Cl based device dropped from 23.5% to 21.8% (~93%) after 1200 hours of aging. In addition, we performed 85 °C aging for the TPPO-based devices which shows superior thermal stability compared to the device without TPPO.
